title: Enterprise Deployments SE - quick reflection
body:
Candidate: Priya Malhotra (resume: enterprise-deployments / ex-cloud-consulting). Interview loop: 60m, panel = me (solutions SE), Maya (security), Ravi (platform eng).

Quick context / why we looped her:
- Strong track record selling/implementing private/VPC deployments at prior company (SaaS -> on-prem transitions).
- Has hands-on experience with network topologies, KMS, HSM integrations, and compliance-heavy customers.
- We needed a pragmatic SE who can translate infra constraints into onboarding plans, plus help with runbooks & early-stage PS engagements.

High-level impression (gut):
- Very effective communicator, asks clarifying questions quickly.
- Deep enough technical understanding to propose concrete mitigations; not a kernel-level expert (fine for SE).
- Comfortable writing runbooks and doing discovery calls.
- Has some gaps around our specific runtime constraints (quantization/kv cache nuance) but adaptable.

Notes from interview (unordered, shorthand):
- Opening: strong framing on prior migrations (multi-week private install for fintech customer). Emphasized network segmentation and least-privilege service account design.
- VPC & networking: walked us through NAT/GW vs. private endpoints tradeoffs. Suggested a two-phase rollout: staging w/ mirrored traffic -> production with explicit egress rules. Good, pragmatic.
- KMS/HSM: implemented customer KMS via cloud provider and did one HSM integration (vendor: Thales) in air-gapped environment. Understood key wrapping, envelope encryption, and rotation cadence. Could describe audit trail needs (who/when/where).
- Air-gapped/on-prem: has done custom packaging (rpm/container images stored on internal registry), offline installer scripts, and signed artifacts. Mentions maintaining a checksum manifest and simple upgrade orchestration (ansible/cust scripts). Practical but not fancy.
- Observability & logging: asks about log ingestion limits and retention. Wants ability to toggle telemetry for onboarding customers (good). Knows basic agent-based tracing but not deep on our tracing hooks - asked if we can provide a minimal tracing shim.
- Security review experience: participated in SOC2 readiness + customer security Q&A decks. Has templates for threat model and third-party questionnaire answers (SIG, ISO-ish).
- Product/Runtime fit: asked direct questions about model pinning, rollback behavior, and graceful degradation. Sees the complexity in supporting mixed-model fallbacks (very aware of customer expectations around latency reliability tradeoffs).
- Pricing/Commercial: comfortable talking through dedicated vs private cost drivers. Good at translating technical constraints to contract terms (eg: SLA tiers, commit sizing).

Behavioral / collaboration notes:
- Clear about working with both sales and eng: prefers to co-own an SOW and then hand off a runbook to platform team.
- Leadership: not trying to be the architect — positions herself as the bridge between customer and internal eng. Likes to drive small POCs early.
- Conflict: described a situation where a customer wanted open outbound access; she mediated and proposed a locked-down proxy with allow-listing and audit logs.

Strengths:
- Customer empathy + technical confidence.
- Deep practical experience with private/on-prem installs and security-origin customers.
- Good runbook/run-level documentation instincts (explicit checklists, smoke tests).

Concerns / gaps:
- Little experience with LLM-serving-specific performance knobs (kv cache details, token-level throughput tuning). She asked clarifying questions but didn’t show deep mental model here.
- Not a software systems engineer by background — more infra/ops + customer-facing. For certain product-embedded SE tasks (writing agent integrations, building runtime patches) might need partner engineering.
- Limited exposure to our specific observability/tracing pipeline (but she can learn).

Level / role-fit suggestion:
- Strong fit for Senior Solutions Engineer / Enterprise SE focusing on Private Deployments and on-prem PS.
- If we expect heavy runtime tuning ownership, consider pairing with Platform/Runtime lead. Works well as customer-facing SE who owns onboarding and SOW delivery.

Score (1-5 scale) across dimensions (quick):
- Technical breadth (infra/security): 4
- Depth on LLM runtime specifics: 2.5
- Customer-facing / communication: 5
- Playbook & PS delivery: 4
- Overall recommended level: Senior SE (IC4-ish)

Hiring recommendation (short):
- Proceed to hire track / final cultural fit loop. Rationale: excellent for the problem we need to solve (private deployments PS), strong SDLC of onboarding, low ramp risk for platform integrations. Missing model-runtime depth but that is teachable and we have runtime engineers to partner.

Follow-ups / questions for onsites / takeaways to ask next interviewer:
- Give a concrete whiteboard: design the onboarding plan for a regulated customer requiring air-gap + FIPS 140-2 HSM. Ask for steps, owners, fallback, and rollback. Evaluate whether candidate can map to our deployment artifacts (k8s manifests, container registries, provisioning scripts).
- Ask for a sample SOW outline for a 3-month private deployment engagement: milestones, deliverables, rollback triggers, acceptance tests.
- Pairing task: walk through a scenario where the customer reports doubled token latency after upgrade — what telemetry would you collect, how would you triage, and what immediate mitigations?

Specific TODOs (my notes):
- Send Priya our private-deployments one-pager and onboarding checklist prior to next loop (link CONFLUENCE).
- Ask Maya to prepare an HSM/crypto deeper question set (Maya knows integration nuance).
- Share a small sample runbook we use for staging -> prod cutover and ask candidate to annotate it during onsite.

Random notes to self (messy):
- She liked the idea of a minimal tracing shim we talked about; maybe add a 2-day spike to PS cadence to build that.
- Good deckable anecdotes for SDRs: “reduced time to first inference by X weeks via mirrored staging + mirrored traffic” — ask her to codify one such case study.

Bottom line: hire-track. Strong customer/infra engineer who will accelerate Private deployments and PS playbook. Not our deepest runtime optimizer, but that is ok for role.
